statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = len(queries) and, for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), r[i] is the length (number of roads traversed) of a shortest directed path from city 0 to city n - 1 in the directed graph G_i with vertices 0, ..., n - 1 and edges {j -> j + 1 | 0 <= j < n - 1} together with {queries[t][0] -> queries[t][1] | 0 <= t <= i}. Shortest means that no directed path from 0 to n - 1 in G_i has smaller length.
preconditions: 3 <= n <= 500; 1 <= len(queries) <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), len(queries[i]) = 2, 0 <= queries[i][0] < queries[i][1] < n, and 1 < queries[i][1] - queries[i][0]; and for all i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(queries), the pair (queries[i][0], queries[i][1]) is different from (queries[j][0], queries[j][1]).
